fx.title: Almost. See the difference
fx.p.は: は marks the topic, what or who you're talking about: わたし は がくせい です.
fx.p.が: が marks who does something or what there is; it goes with あります, います, すき and after だれ or なに.
fx.p.を: を marks the object of the action, what you eat, drink or see: みず を のみます.
fx.p.に: に marks the destination, the time, or where something is: にほん に いきます.
fx.p.で: で marks where an action happens, or the means: でんしゃ で いきます.
fx.p.へ: へ marks the direction you're heading; like に with いきます, but stressing direction.
fx.p.の: の joins two nouns, like «'s»: わたし の なまえ is «my name».
fx.p.も: も means «too» and takes the place of は, が or を.
fx.p.と: と means «and» between nouns, or «with» someone.
fx.p.か: か at the end turns the sentence into a question.
fx.order: The tiles are right; change the order.
fx.orderVerb: The tiles are right; change the order. In Japanese the verb (or です) goes last.
